Maybe some are satisfied with sustenance and others expect an exceptional experience; either way, kudos for a valiant effort.
reviews.author: JKtravel S.

reviews.text: They should put that Dover Sole brown butter sauce on everything.  The Dover Sole was delish but once we drenched it in the bitter sauce it was just perfection.  Add a small crouton on top and it is to die for.  We even took the filet mignon and drenched the Dover sole sauce on that and it made the filet 100x better.  And the asparagus.  The tuna tartare appetizer was also quite unique.  Overall it showed me something new.
reviews.author: Tommy C.

reviews.text: The manager Patrick is not a five star hotel employee. He belongs somewhere else. Don't go there if you plan to be treated well.
reviews.author: Rhonda B.

reviews.text:
I just returned from another dinner at J and G steakhouse. This is probably at a minimum the eighth time I have been there. We used to eat at Mary Elaine's  and continued dining in the same spot at the Phoenician resort. This without question, cannot be considered fine dining! The last two dining experiences have been ruined by incredibly ill behaved tables near us. Shouting screaming and clapping and yelling. As it is that makes the atmosphere go straight downhill. The service is always slow and splotchy at best but the food is good. After an hour and a half of deafening noise from the savages we finally had about 15 minutes of peace and quiet and then asked for the check. We just wanted to leave a soon as possible because it was not an enjoyable experience. The waiter came by and we said bring us the check and gave him our credit card. He then took the credit card returned with a slip of paper which we signed and I went to the front desk to retrieve our leftovers while my wife was in the bathroom. The waiter frantically ran up to me and told me that I didn't sign any credit card slip. He was basically accusing me of trying to walk out. We then asked them to check and see what we signed. We couldn't imagine what we signed because we gave them the card, they left with it and returned to our table. It turned out that they gave us a room slip to sign and did not run our credit card. That is not our fault. I asked for the manager and a snooty young girl claimed she was the manager. She then chose talk over me every second that she could without listening to the crux of what I was saying. It is the servers issue if he did not run our credit card properly when we gave it to him. Then to have him run up to us as we were leaving like we are crooks is not acceptable. I tried to explain this and was talked down to and talked over every second I opened my mouth. When you combine the miserable atmosphere with being spoken to in such a rude and disrespectful manner by an untrained person it is easy to conclude that you will be taking yourself elsewhere for dinners. As we usually do our bill came to over $300. You have to ask yourself where can I go and relax and enjoy find food and not be treated like a second-class citizen writing a public bus. I attempted to explain to this supposed manager what the issue was and then I'd have decided it was time to leave when my wife said this is useless let's go. This ill behaved intern then turned and started spouting off to the my back as I walked away. At which point I gave her a few expletives and decided to leave for good.

In short you cannot find a worse place to spend such a large amount of money and then be treated rudely. I invite the management to search my reservation and phone number and then see exactly how many times I've been a repeat customer. There is no excuse for having such incompetence in running a restaurant and allowing the atmosphere to deteriorate to that of a second rate bar. No one in the hospitality industry should ever ever talk back to a guest to the back of their head as they walk away. If you're going to be rude and disrespectful at least have the Courage to do it right to the customers face.
reviews.author: Robert B.

reviews.text: Amazing. The view is stunning and the meat was cooked perfectly! Do mash potatoes as a side! Oh and the truffle... to die for!
reviews.author: Briana B.

reviews.text: This is a wonderful restaurant. The ambiance is magical- perfect for a romantic dinner. We had the chopped salad, prime rib, creamed spinach, and potatoes. The service was 5 star.
reviews.author: L J.

reviews.text:
This review is for the Thanksgiving Day Brunch

High end gluttonous delight resulting in a food coma is how I would describe my experience. Beyond expectation, this feast was incredibly delicious, comfortable and I did not regret paying $125 per person for this experience. Staff let us dine at a leisurely pace and attentively kept our beverages full while we enjoyed our feast over looking the balcony.

I decided to forgo most of the traditional offerings and pursued the caviar, raw bar and far fattier and less healthy options such as deep fried quail (delicious), pork belly, and no less than 6 desserts. 

Luckily, the newly renovated lobby was a nice place to digest before heading home for Black Friday shopping. As every outing to the Phoenician, this was a truly memorable event and always fun and relaxing.
reviews.author: Tricia K.

reviews.text:
Make reservations.  Order the tuna tartare.  Order a few more tuna tartares.  Enjoy the chic vibe and the sparkling Phoenix skyline at nighttime.  Return many times.  Savor the opportunities to return for more tuna tartare.  Tuna tartare.
In all seriousness, J & G Steakhouse is a beautiful gem of a restaurant in Phoenix, more specifically at the Phoenician Resort.  This is a great choice for a romantic and quiet dinner or a special occasion.  The service is excellent, and the atmosphere is wonderful:  there is cool music, fire pits on the balcony, and stunning views.  The tuna tartare is easily in my top 3 lifelong culinary experiences.  This restaurant is one I recommend to anyone visiting or living in Phoenix.
reviews.author: Inessa F.

reviews.text: I just wanted to write about my experience at J&G Steakhouse.  My mom is visiting from Wisconsin, and we wanted to take her out for a nice birthday dinner and were excited to take her to J&G. The lady at the check-in desk was wonderful, as usual, and welcomed us.  My husband and I have dined at J&G multiple times so she recognized us and was warm and welcome. I thought it would be a good indication of the rest of our time there, but that wasn't the case. Our waiter was really bad, when he initially came to take our order, we said we would need another minute; he came back approximately 20 minutes later.  Throughout the evening, we barely saw him, and toward the end of our meal, once our plates were cleared, and he knew we were finished and ready to go, we sat there for probably another 20-30 minutes waiting for our check.  It was so bad that we contemplated getting up and asking the front desk for our check instead. We came in right at opening, and it was not that busy. The worst part is he was focused on the table right beside us, and it was pretty obvious he was showing them preferential treatment. My husband and I asked the waiter if the chicken Parmesan were enough for my husband and I to split since we were already getting an appetizer, he said yes, so we did.  My husband's portion was not good at all, and he was surprised that J&G would serve chicken like it. He had the dark chicken thigh portion, and I had the white chicken, he said the chicken thigh tasted like school cafeteria meat and he could barely stomach it. I had to give him some of my white chicken, so he would not be hungry. The waiter never came to ask how our food was, and was so absent that my husband had to resort to drinking ice water throughout the rest of the meal because he never came to check on refills. My mom ordered a glass of wine, once that was gone, he never asked if she wanted another one. I asked for a window seat in my reservation, which I made weeks ago, and we weren't seated in front of the window. I have been planning my mom's birthday dinner for weeks since she is only in town for a short time, and I was really hoping J&G would go above and beyond my expectations, I will definitely be picking a different place next time. Obviously the new management that took over the Phoenician do not care about their customers.  I wrote them over a week ago with my experience and they never responded, the old management cared about the service they provided and if there was a problem, they reached out and did things to rectify the situation so they wouldn't lose customers.
reviews.author: Shawna A.

reviews.text:
Steaks cooked perfectly! Service was fantastic! Desserts are a must. J&G has a nice, dim, intimate vibe. We had prime seating by the windows overlooking the Phoenician pool and Scottsdale skyline. 

As far as food selection, we ordered filet med rare and the Brussels. Steak was delicious with the bernaise sauce (cooked grilled.)  Brussels were bland, probably wouldn't order again. For dessert we had apple crisp and cheesecake. Both straightforward desserts. Cheesecake was very light and refreshing. Crisp was rich, tart and decadently sweet. 

Overall 5 for ambiance, solid food and service.
reviews.author: Pam S.

reviews.text:
My wife and I make it an absolute priority to stop in for drinks and small plates whenever we visit Phoenix so this was going to be our typical check on the list for the evening.  That is, until we were thrown for a loop.  We usually opt for the Thirsty Camel since it's great for people watching and the atmosphere is upbeat rather than typical hotel lounges which will put you to sleep fast.  Well, that went out the window due to them renovating the entire area including the main entrance.  So now what?

Our driver dropped us at the other entrance and we had to make a decision.  Do we leave and go to Mastro's or start at J & G?  We opted for the latter and it was a great decision. I have been to this city for the better part of 27 years and I have never been to this place mainly because I had a destination always planned out ahead of time.  

The visuals are stunning to start off with.  It has an wide view of the entire valley, the lounge itself is well put together and the restaurant is gorgeous.  We always tend to opt for the bar when we are going out for a night on the town since we gravitate towards small plates and the more immediate service aspect rather than the full presentation.  Brian was taking care of us and he was on point.  Very conversational, attentive and we felt 100% taken care of.  A lot of bartenders will give you the small talk and it's somewhat canned and then presented in a way that makes you feel if you come back the next night, it's the same exact interaction verbatim.  He was not that way at all.  

I opted for the Pinot Blanc and then a glass of Pinot Grigio while my wife had the Brut Rose'.  Both were excellent.  The appetizers were what really shined here though.  The shrimp cocktail was perfect.  The chill was exactly what you want and the size were quite large.  The Tuna Tartare' was just ok in our opinion.  It was missing something but it wasn't bad.  It could be that we just enjoyed the other items more.  

The appetizer that blew my mind though was the Crispy Calamari.  I have to preface the fact that I am not a calamari person by nature but this was off the grid in terms of a great dish.  It's almost impossible to get calamari to be crispy, flaky and not have it be overly greasy or rubbery.  Well, they did just that.  It had a consistency that I have never experienced.  It was so good that we ordered it again.  That's about as common for me as having a Vegan try a Bone-In Ribeye and then order another.  

The music which was provided was a nice addition without being overly loud to where we couldn't hear ourselves talk.  The sum it up, I think The Thirsty Camel lost two customers and J & G gained two.  This has nothing to do with the former but everything to do with the latter.  It's hard to go wrong either way.
reviews.author: Charles C.

reviews.text: This is the restaurant at the Phoenician. The view was really nice and the food is excellent as you would expect from a five-star hotel. I had the five Peppercorn steak potato and the cream spinach. You may want to stay away from the cream spinach if you're used to eating at Applebee'sas this cream that they use in the spinach is really really good and not like you would find in a typical chain restaurant. Anyway, I recommend it especially if you're at the hotel.
reviews.author: Scott D.

reviews.text: The hostess team needs to get their story straight. Said we could not be seated in the restaurant for 1.25 hours due to other reservations yet we could count on two hands the amount of open tables (it's Mid June) and hotel is undergoing renovation for goodness sake! Silver lining - Brian @ JG bar was Terrific and one-man band was great and we met a really fun couple. Interesting the hostess team also said that we are  not serving food on the patio and yet we came out with our cocktail after dinner and there was a couple wrapping up their Anniversary meal. REALLY!???
reviews.author: Mary C.

reviews.text:
It's hard to decide which was worse - the service or the food. 
Went to celebrate a birthday, restaurant was notified in advance of this. Small party of only 4 of us. 
Waited 30 minutes to get our salads, they cleared the plates and then we never saw our server again for 45 more minutes.
Finally the food arrived. The salmon came completely raw. The scallops were fine until squeezing the lemon that came on the plate with them, which had some sort of rancid chemical taste.
So, half of us had to send back our meals. Did a manager come to apologize or check on us? Nope! Waited another 20 minutes before a human being came to the table again. Not our server but flagged down some girl working there, told her we wanted the check. Took another 20 minutes of just sitting there until that happened.
reviews.author: Stefany M.

reviews.text:
Dined here during Restaurant Week, Spring 2017.

Food was amazing. Had fresh oysters along with cocktails and beer prior to the appetizers.

I couldn't get enough of the gazpacho; it was so flavorful and with a surprising kick to it. Also tried the angel hair, which I initially thought was odd to serve as a starter, but it was so good. The noodles were definitely fresh and the pesto was so good. I was definitely blown away by the appetizer dishes.

The sea bass was also enjoyable. The couscous looked dry at first but I was proven wrong with the first try, along with the tomatoes had such a good tang to them. The fish was nicely cooked. The flavors worked really well together. Overall, it was a well constructed dish with such good, solid flavors. Also tried the grilled flat iron, which was ordered medium rare, but came out within the medium-medium well range. It was good, but I was expecting more from a steakhouse.

Dessert was solid. Had the lava and cheesecake. Pretty good.

Service was great. I would definitely return again to explore the rest of the menu, along with that gazpacho.
reviews.author: Roselle A.

reviews.text: Great food, service, and view! I had one of the best steaks in my life here. The pairing sauces are simply delicious! If I'm ever back in the area, I will come back here for sure!
reviews.author: Monica D.

reviews.text: We went here last year for our anniversary dinner, and it was so amazing! The service was incredible and so was the food. I've never been so full, but I couldn't stop eating ;) the parmesan crusted chicken was delicious, and they even treated us to an anniversary dessert, just because they happened to ask why we were coming in that night!
reviews.author: Ashley M.

reviews.text: What a terrific location, great food, exceptional service. Gregory was absolutely spot-on in his timing.  Impeccable service by a man meant to do this job here.  Cocktails were perfect, view was all you could ask for with Camelback "right there".  Steak was prepared perfectly, salad and dessert were great.  A bit pricey, but for that special night out, this place can't be beat.
reviews.author: David C.

reviews.text: Our experience was unfortunate. We chose to eat dinner at the bar - which wasn't crowded at all - 6-8 people. We ordered 2 martinis, gave us three because "they didn't have their regular glasses", poured them over the bar and spilled all over. Then handed us our brown paper placemats so we could set our own place setting. We expected a different experience as guests at the hotel. Bread didn't come until we asked for it - 30 minutes later, with dinner. The bartender - Brian - who came on once she left - salvaged our experience (as best he could). Kyle who carved our steak was great. When my husband spoke with the 20 something year old Manager - she trivialized his concerns and offered no remedy. The musician was great. We've been here 2 nights, 4 to go.....?
reviews.author: Katie P.

reviews.text:
We stayed at the Phoenician for our honeymoon and picked J & G for our 'big' celebratory meal. Service was fine, but almost too casual for the upscale-steakhouse feel and especially for the price tag. 
The food left a lot to be desired. The steaks were fine (we're from Texas so maybe that's why we weren't super impressed), the sides were ok, but the steak sauces (especially the J&G signature steak sauce) were not very good. 
We were treated to a free congratulatory dessert that was so so kind of them and really delicious, so that left our night on a high note, but we were overall disappointed with the food and atmosphere for how much it cost.
reviews.author: Kelsey M.

reviews.text: J & Gs is my favorite restaurant in Phoenix. The view is so pretty of the grounds and sky/stars being up on the top floor. The service is excellent except had to wait a long time in the bar area for a server for a before dinner drink. Your typical steak house fare. They have a great shrimp cocktail and their oysters are loved by my son. Really nice wine selection by the bottle. Parker House rolls to die for. Great ambience - food good. And the musician this past Saturday night was really good!!
reviews.author: Sarah L.

reviews.text:
The fact this restaurant rates so high is perplexing, but I am more surprised Jean Georges has an affiliation.  The price is definitely JG, but the quality and menu are lacking. 

So, first what I liked: Staff were friendly and generally attentive. The view is nice.  The veal chop was excellent.   The sauces were good as well.

However, two people at our table ordered steak, one rare and the other medium rare, but they both came out rare.  Cardinal sin.  There is no fixing this situation.  If it is sent back everyone else has to stop and let their food get cold or finish their meal by the time the steak returns.

The bigger issue at this restaurant is the antiquated menu.  Straight out of the 80's. Tuna tartar, crab cakes and fried calamari?? You're joking, right? What they couldn't squeeze coconut shrimp or potato skins on the menu?

What's worse the plating has zero appeal. Look at some of the pictures in other posts, specifically the pork belly.  Basic.  It also was not very good - If this were the first meat dish I had, I would be a vegan.  The steaks were placed on the plate with 3 peppers, no thought at all.  I am not asking for a blooming onion on each plate, but for the price it needs to look better than Outback.

As I said before, the people were friendly and that goes a long-long way, but to be accurate there were points in the evening where I felt forgotten.  If everything else were on point I might ignore this oversight, but it wasn't and for the price this should never be the case.

Lastly,  the Phoenician and J&G need about a $40m-$50m remodel.  This place felt tired.  

Change the menu, remodel the restaurant and give me a reason to come back.
reviews.author: Vic R.

reviews.text:
Staying at the Phoenician and looking for an offsite dinner, we had a tire blow out and opted for a night in.  Great choice!  While not perfect, (in spite of my 5 star review), the food was outstanding.  I was leaning toward fish, but the waiter described the steak and I was in. One of THE best I've ever had.  I like a steak medium well and often I have chefs try to give me a lesser grade option thinking I do t know what I'm talking about.  But this was PERFECT!  Perfectly seasoned (not too salty), perfectly cooked.  And I LOVED the sauces.  LOVED!  I can't say I had a favorite.  So good. 

Other winners were snap peas (with mi t and ginger) which were other-worldly and beets.  My wife opted for Tina taretar as an entree and loved that.   Toffee pudding was ridiculous!  

The only "miss" was the four gras appetizer which was delicious but inexplicably served with a tart rhubarb purée.  The rhubarb sounded good but so over-powered and disappointed that we opted to forego it altogether Bd just do the pate with toast.  Really good. But in my humble opinion, a sweeter option would have made this as good as the rest of the meal.  

Drinks were great a an excellent wine menu.  The place is a must!  

Shoutout to bartender Brian, who made excellent drinks and listened to us.  And to Chris, who backed up our waiter and was just excellent!
reviews.author: Jon N.

reviews.text:
J & G needs to work on their service - big time.  We ordered the tasting menu.   Each course was unceremoniously dumped at the table.  First three courses in soup bowls.  Little to no plating involved and difficult to eat from.   The server gave us NO explanations, NO presentation s--- I Iooked at my food, and just thought "What is this?"  Our steaks, ordered medium rare, came out well done.  When we called the server, his comment ' "Well, I can't really see them."  He did bring out new sides for us since ours were now cold.  The tartar -good.  Seafood - good, well seared.  Steak - been there, but the vegetable side (I'm not sure what it was because again - no presentation - very good.  Dessert - lava cake good, ice cream - no flavor.  
I don't like to give negative reviews, but this meal was expensive - I expected more.
reviews.author: Judy C.

reviews.text: Outdoor patio seating, great wine list and cocktails, excellent food with breathtaking views
reviews.author: Paula V.

reviews.text: We celebrated my mother's birthday at J & G's in Scottsdale.  The food was absolutely delicious, perfectly prepared, the view of the Valley of the Sun, spectacular, the service surpassed any I have ever experienced.  From the moment we were seated, Patrick Norton and Team made this a most memorable event.  :-)
reviews.author: Debbi S.

reviews.text:
Have stayed at the Phoenician on numerous occasions and finally had dinner here.
Romantic ambiance with extraordinary city lights and has a outside patio with fire-pits which add to the views. Very nice long bar, well stocked with premium labels.  Martinis served in old fashioned round martini/champagne glasses. Perfect Sapphire dry martini.
The Jumbo prawn appetizer was a little limp, passable but expected better from this 5 star restaurant....maybe difficult to fly in fresh prawns on a daily basis.
However, everything else was perfect and the aged Ribeye exceeded my expectations. You will not be disappointed. Very flavorful, aged, grass fed and lean but very tender. Selected the Faust. A big red cab out of Napa.  Probably the best value on the extensive wine list and it came in a split so you can enjoy more than 1 wine label. BTW, If you are fan of Quintessa....its in the family.
The standard sides are shareable so just have each person order 1 side and share.  The cheese au gratin  is like candy.  The Cinnamon Apple Crumb was the coup de grau paired with a 10 yr old Port.
Kudos to Jeff........superb service.
Definitely go again......would have given 5 stars but the shrimp........
reviews.author: Jon G.

reviews.text:
Unfortunately this place is overrated, we ordered three apps and three entrees... the steak was not too quality and didn't have much flavor, the salmon was eovercooked (we ordered it med rare and received it well done) I had the sole and it was great. However, when the server took back the salmon to have a new one prepared he didn't offer to keep the other foods warm while the salmon was cooking (so we ate cold entrees) when the manager brought the new salmon back to the table she apologized but didn't offer to comp a dessert for our troubles or even really express concern for our tables now cold other entrees. The apps were ok, we had the black truffle cheese fritters and those were pretty disappointing and lacked flavor. We also had the tuna tartare, again very disappointing kind of soggy and just not appetizing. Lastly we ordered the pork belly, again, flavorless and nothing life changing. Overall, the best part of the dinner was the service and view inside and out of the restaurant, probably would not go back. 

Side note, after writing this review and sending a complaint to the manager he was very kind asked the best time to call me and speak about the situation. He never called and never attempted to contact me. Clearly the terrible customer service starts at the top.
reviews.author: Betania V.

reviews.text:
Birthday dinner at this well respected steak house.  I'm going to make my review straightforward and simple.

Environment:  5 stars  Contemporary elegant setting 
Welcoming:    5 stars
Service:         5 stars (Candace our server was great; checked on us frequently)  Manager came around and even filled our water glasses.  Everyone is hands-on.

Food:  
     French onion soup                 5 stars
     Amazing parker house rolls    5 stars
     Veal chop so thick and juicy and perfectly prepared:  5 stars
     Steak with frites:   2 stars-------- an average piece of steak; I can't say the meat was delicious.      Frites were fine.  
    Spinach (sauteed):  2 stars------ No distinctive flavor despite being told that the spinach had herbs in it, including mint. (could not discern the mint)   We cut up the small roasted peppers which accompanied the veal chop and added it to the spinach along with peppercorn sauce and certainly improved the flavor.  (Did I just cook on my birthday?) 

Sauces:  4 stars---they provided 3 sauces to choose from to enhance the flavors of the meats.
Dessert:   4 stars----Chocolate molten cake with caramel ice cream.   Chocolate cake was not cloyingly sweet.  Nice!
reviews.author: Yvonne G.

reviews.text: Very disappointing. We went to the Phoenician with friends be able to site outside and enjoy the evening since the resort does have fabulous views of the Valley from patio beyond the lobby. We decided while there to have dinner at J&G. This is a beautiful restaurant also with great views of the Valley and can be a very romantic spot to dine with its dim lighting and soft live music. Also the service is good but that's where it ends. It is certainly overpriced for what you get. After reviewing the wine list we decided to stick with sparkling water. I've gotten Dr. Loosens Riesling in plenty of restaurants in the Valley but never have I seen it cost $48.00 for a 1/2 bottle (2 glasses according to our waiter) that alone is ridiculous. My husband and I had the chopped salad and I have had much better chopped salads, it was just mediocre at best consisting of a few greens, apple that could have been cut smaller and a few pecans on top and a little too peppery for my liking even the dressing was underwhelming. There was even nothing  special about the popover rolls and normally the bread is one of my favorite parts of dining out! I ordered an 8oz filet medium rare and it was almost medium well, they did take it back but it took quite sometime before the waiter returned with another steak by then everyone was done eating; at least it was medium rare this time. Their signature sauces were okay but really not necessary when you have a good steak. If this is such a great steakhouse they should have gotten right from the beginning. My husband and I shared the Brussels sprouts which were also nothing special, again it had a few pecans sprinkled on top. If I'm going to drop $200 on dinner there is no reason to return here when we have some great steakhouses like Mastros, City Hall Steakhouse, Dominick's, Capital Grille or Fleming's to just name a few in the Scottsdale/Phoenix area.
reviews.author: Denise M.

reviews.text: I am going to commend J&G steakhouse for stellar food, great view and fond memories. My boyfriend and I had our first date here. I was blown away by the ambiance and view and by the way the staff handled our night. We had such a wonderful experience that we came back the year after for our anniversary. The cherry on top was that the waiter came out with an anniversary cake (chocolate cake with fruit and ice cream, I believe). Now, we come at times just to get desserts. I recommend the baked Alaska and their risotto. Also, their complementary bread is to die for!
reviews.author: Camille D.

reviews.text:
A stalwart: outstanding ambience, superlative service and delicious fare. What else can a foodie want. 
The Caesar Salad was tossed to perfection: just the right hint of anchovies, succulent and firm greens and a delicious dressing. The 16 ounce Lamb T-Bone: a home run! I usually am a 8 to 12 ounce guy. This one I wolfed down in record time. 
This place rocks!
reviews.author: Harris M.

reviews.text: We were here for brunch and what a gorgeous backdrop...the entire valley. Jean the manager was attentive and hospitable. Breakfast offered a yummy omelet bar, juices, potatoes, bacon, pastries, fruit, and cereals...hot coffee, etc. Overall a fabulous breakfast.
reviews.author: Bunny G.

reviews.text: It was a little bit pricy  it it was worth it. The service was great and everybody didn't miss a beat . The dinner is something I will always remember
reviews.author: Food Porn A.

reviews.text:
We booked a private room for 35 guests in the sunset room and patio. What a gorgeous room, from the decor to the furniture!

The minute you step in, J&G Steakhouse's customer service and ambiance set the the tone for the evening.

Food overall was pretty solid.

I ordered:
1) Butternut squash soup: 4/5 this was really well made
2) Sweet and sour beet risotto: 1/5 it was a really strange and unusual dish for me. 
3) Bison Ribeye: 3.5/5 I expected more, but it was just OK.
4) Warm Chocolate Cake: 3.5/5 good, but not amazing since it was typical chocolate cake. At an establishment like this, you would thing they would do a twist or creative approach to chocolate cake.
reviews.author: Jen H.

reviews.text: My recent visit was fantastic.  Excellent service and the food was wonderful.  I definitely want to come back!
reviews.author: Jody C.

reviews.text: Came up to the top floor and saw the amazing skyline. We were seated quickly. The dark atmosphere made this place classy. We really were looking forward to this meal. Staff was very friendly but the food was not seasoned and just wasn't good; considering how expensive the food was. I don't think we will be back, there are just so many restaurants, so little vacation time. I would rather eat somewhere with better food.
reviews.author: Tanya P.

reviews.text: We have been to J and G Steakhouse several times due to the location and great view. We usually always order two nice bottles of wine and full course dinners for our family. We decided to make a reservations a month ago and have 5 adults for dinner on Thanksgiving. We had a 5:45 reservations as service started around 5 pm on Thanksgiving at J and G. Something was really off with the service! We did the pre-set Thanksgiving meal at 65 dollars per person. The dinner was ok but not great as turkey was dry. It was as if we were forgotten. No one even made a pass by our table once our main dish was served. No offer of coffee or after dinner drinks. No sign of our desert which was included. After 15 minutes with dishes sitting in front of us with no one coming by to collect we finally stood up walking to the patio outside and requested to someone walking to notify our server we were requesting our desert to be brought to patio. A gal, not our server, who looked like she may have been helping in kitchen delivered the deserts outside another 15 minutes later. No offer of coffee or after dinner drinks. We saw the manager, Patrick, walking around but found it odd he was not noticing the lack of service at several tables....mainly ours. Under staffed? Not sure but they clearly knew in advanced how many people had reservations. Disappointed. Expect more from a restaurant who aspires to be top notch.
reviews.author: Cindy C.

reviews.text:
Too much peppercorn! Both in my salmon and the Caesar salad. Watching the promotional spot in our room, the chef confesses to using peppercorn, but I found it too overpowering. 
My wife's filet was delicious. It was served with sauces but needed none. 
Our server was professional, but stiff. The bus-girl was very courteous and efficient.
Live music was a nice touch. Great views.
reviews.author: Frank B.

reviews.text: My husband and I are serious steak snobs. We lived in NYC for many years and now live in the Bay Area, so we've tried them all. Also, my husband makes an incredible steak. So, it takes a lot to impress us. J&G did just that. We were in a bit of a rush, as we were trying to have a "quick" steak dinner before catching a flight back to SF. The service was great, they were very accommodating. I was actually a little concerned that some corners would be cut because we were rushing, but it was pure perfection. We got a bone-in ribeye and a bone-in filet. Temperature was spot on, flavors were impeccable. All in all, I can't wait to go back!
reviews.author: Shara C.

reviews.text: We have had dinner several times at this restaurant, and attempted to enjoy it again there a year ago and so looked forward to it.  (We were bringing friends, and had talked about it so much over the years).  The service was beyond disappointing.  We waited 45 minutes to be seated  although we had reservations ( and had asked to be seated outside when we made the reservations) only to be seated next to the private room where a very loud party was going on.  We asked to be moved outside...we were accommodated, and it was odd that few of the tables were being used.  We got a half baked explanation about wait stations, etc.  The food was fine, but not exceptional. The bill was enormous for the experience.  Our friends have not stopped talking about how disappointed they were.  Sadly, we are about to make our yearly trip from New York to Scottsdale again, and for the first time we will not be returning to this restaurant
reviews.author: Pamela D.

reviews.text:
Wonderful staff all around. Great food all around. Loved the atmosphere and the view. Outdoor seating with gas fire pits are wonderful. 

The sides for sharing for 5 people were a bit small. Once a side went around the table they were done. 

Huge wine selection and bar had several fun cocktails.
reviews.author: Anna P.

reviews.text: We recently tried this place for our anniversary.  We had been looking at the Restaurant Week selections online and their menu looked appealing.   We made a reservation through the website and included that it was our anniversary.  We arrived and self parked, which is a bit of an adventure with the required changing of elevators.  The restaurant is lovely and we asked to be seated outside.  The view is very nice and the atmosphere was pleasant.  Our waiter was excellent, sorry I didn't get his name, absolutely perfect service.  We chose the Restaurant Week menu which had an appetizer, entree and dessert for each of us.  I had the butternut squash salad, salmon and the apple crumble.  Quite simply some of the best I have ever had anywhere!  That salad was just incredible, I could have made an entire meal of just a giant one!  My salmon was yummy with some tasty Brussels sprouts and mashed potatoes.  The apple crumble is so good you wish you were more hungry cause it's kinda big.  Husband enjoyed his shrimp, steak and chocolate cake as much as I loved mine.  They gave us a nice card and brought us complementary champagne too.   A lovely evening and we will be back!
reviews.author: Sharen B.

reviews.text: My husband and I had dinner at this wonderful Steak House at the Phoenician Resort on Saturday evening September 17, 2016. Our Waiter was David and his assistant Chris O.  Our service was amazing and the food wonderful.  Chris O was very attentive and made our experience at this restuarant awesome.  I highly recommend this Steak House and suggest that you ask for both David and Chris O to be your servers.  Thanks for a wonderful evening, Marion and David
reviews.author: Marion M.

reviews.text:
We love the Phoenician but service at this steakhouse sucks. This is our second time eating in the bar. Great ambiance, great view...

We sat in the bar both times because cool environment, but we had the same bar tender wait on us and we felt like we were an inconvenience to her even though we were the only couple in the bar.  She was more interested in talking with her fellow employees than helping  us. Hopefully when Marriot takes this over, she will not be here . 

On the reverse side, Ahmet in the lobby bar is awesome and is doing a great job with his staff
reviews.author: David H.

reviews.text: My boyfriend and I are locals and decided to pick a nice place with a view for our date night. $260 dollars later we could not be more dissatisfied. It was the worst customer experience we have dealt with in a long time. We were constantly greeted with a new server that couldn't remember what we already ordered or when we ordered it. To top this off the food was no where near its past reputation. What a shame. We will not be back
reviews.author: A H.

reviews.text: Generally the food is reliably good. The service can good but my experience is that the highly qualified bus staff and food runners are def better than the servers. The server Christian, was friendly to other tables but non challant with us and other tables. He seemed to be trying to listen in on our conversation. Quite annoying. The last time the food had some issues but the manager and staff have no interest in satisfying the customer
reviews.author: Bill W.

reviews.text: What a beautiful place atop the Phoenician resort. My Miso Carmelized filet was spicy and unique I loved it. The chilled lobster was fantastic as well as the French Onion Soup.
reviews.author: Steven J.

reviews.text: Our waiter had a lot to be desired, never came around. Cris O saved us, bringing us sour cream, coffee, butter. Chris O deserves a raise or /and promotion. The food was good, but not as we had hoped.
reviews.author: Suzanne D.

reviews.text: My husband and I had the most perfect evening last night at J & G Steakhouse.  The dining room is spectacular and our table allowed us to both face the expansive window and enjoy the breathtaking view.  Our server, Zach Moore, provided us with impeccable service.  He made great recommendations and was extremely attentive.  The food was fabulous.  The steaks were cooked to perfection and the sides were amazing.  Dessert was to die for!  We had the pleasure of meeting Taylor Chandler, the Assistant GM, who was very professional and also provided another great layer of hospitality.  If you are in the Phoenix area, you do not want to miss this superb dining experience!
reviews.author: Nancy C.

reviews.text:
The food is amazing, first class. The service is excellent. The atmosphere and view are incredible. I really couldn't find a complaint.

We had the calamari appetizer and it was prepared perfectly and is paired with an incredible sauce. For our mains, we had the prime ribeye Oscar style (which I would highly recommend) and it was the nicest cut of meat I think I've ever had, and the crab and asparagus just took it to the next level. We had a nice bottle of Merlot with our meal. And shared a sticky toffee pudding for dessert, which was also amazing.

There service was attentive without being intrusive. It was really fantastic, the entire dining experience.
reviews.author: Laura G.

reviews.text: My wife and I stopped there the other night and enjoyed tuna tar tar.  Thank you Chris O. You are the best!!!
reviews.author: Thomas B.

reviews.text: We did a staycation at the Phoenician and tried this restaurant one night.  The only reason I'm giving it three stars is because you can't ignore the view and all of the problems we had were recognized, owned and dealt with immediately by the Manager, Pat.  The service was the worst we've had at any restaurant.  Our drink glasses were removed and we weren't offered a refill or another drink.  They ran out of dinner rolls and offered us burnt sourdough toast (for real).  The food took forever to come out of the kitchen.  When it finally arrived, three our of four meals were wonderful.  We understand that a kitchen can be slow, but have the waitstaff who can offer customers the opportunity to not notice, by being kind and personable and apologetic rather than rude and afraid to talk to your table.  We would probably give it another try just once.
reviews.author: T L.

reviews.text: I was told there were better steakhouses, but we still wanted to see the views that this place was known for. Our service was terrible partly because our server had too many tables (7 or 8 tables is a lot to handle and give good service). We waited 25 minutes before our server took our drink order. The quality of food was average at best. I am not a "salt" person and never need - or want - to add salt when I'm eating a restaurant. Most of the food needed salt!! The $35 halibut was boring and bland - literally it had no flavor. The steak was ok (expect for the fact that it wasn't cooked the way I ordered it). The server never asked how our food was until it was time to clear our plates. He didn't even great us when we arrived so I didn't get his name. The best part and the reason for the 2nd star was the the warm chocolate cake we had for dessert. Don't waste your time or money. Overall, under spiced and over priced!
reviews.author: R K.

reviews.text: Food is very good, but not worth the prices. You can find better steaks for less money. The tuna tartar though is a little slice of bliss! Great wine selection, but for the $$ it better be! Nice place for special occasions and if you have an extra couple of hundred dollars burning a hole in your pocket. Service is a little stuffy. Great views.
reviews.author: Bud B.

reviews.text: The View is stunning, The Service was Outstanding, The FOOD was delicious and I'm excited to go back....after telling a plethora of friends ! Beautiful evening, great company
reviews.author: Deni B.

reviews.text:
I went here for my 21st birthday and had a wonderful experience! I was with my dad and my boyfriend. We had a reservation and were seated right when we got there. At the table there was a little happy birthday card waiting for me! I thought that was a very nice touch. 

I ordered the asparagus risotto as an appetizer. It was green in color which I've never seen before but it was absolutely delicious! My dad ordered the baby beet salad as an appetizer and said it was great. For my entree, I got the 12oz Filet Mignon. And let me tell you, this was probably the BEST piece of steak I've ever had in my life. It was perfectly cooked Medium and extremely tender. It almost just melted in my mouth. The taste was phenomenal. My dad ordered the Halibut and said it was very good. My boyfriend ordered the rib eye and didn't leave anything left on his plate! For sides, we ordered the mashed potatoes, broccoli, and snap peas. They were all super tasty! 

After we finished our meals, I was treated to a complimentary chocolate lava cake. It was amazing! Best chocolate lava cake I've ever had. 

OVERALL:
The service here was prompt, attentive and organized. Overall, I would 100% recommend this restaurant to anyone. If you're looking for a nice meal to celebrate an occasion or just to go out for a good dinner, this is definitely the place to go!
reviews.author: Olivia M.

reviews.text:
I went for a business dinner, and this place was quite good.  The tasting menu at $63 was a fantastic value.  Came with: Tuna tartare, asparagus risotto, crispy halibut, and filet.  The food portions were generous considering it was a tasting menu (6oz each fish and steak) and everything was well prepared.  

The one thing was that the service in the bar area felt understaffed, and wait times were long to get seated, get a drink, water, etc.  But, that wasn't the end of the world.
reviews.author: Mike A.

reviews.text:
Price - 3 stars. This is a steakhouse. So the price is what you would expect

Service - 4 stars. Absolutely great service!! Our drinks was always refilled promptly and the food came out fast. However, I never knew my server name!! He never said his name!! So when I needed extra sauce....I would actually like to call a person by their name.

Food - 2 stars. I ordered the Tomahawk steak, I ordered it medium but came out med rare. Also the French onion soup was VERY salty, and the halibut was bland.

Atmosphere - 3 stars. The view was beautiful; however, the place was busy and it was small, the server and customers was constantly "bumping" into my guest seat, which made her uncomfortable.
reviews.author: Peter N.

reviews.text:
Overall amazing!

My husband and I went to J&G and enjoyed the tasting menu with the wine pairings. The food was delicious and the wines paired really well. The staff is so friendly and knowledgeable that I felt they went above and beyond to make us feel like we were their only priority. Highly recommend and we will be back again!! Thank you!
reviews.author: Liz K.

reviews.text:
I've provided the same review on OpenTable, and will also post on TripAdvisor. My wife and I celebrated our 25th anniversary @ J&G, and our dinner was spectacular. In a city with a reputation as a world-class resort/vacation destination, and with an abundance of superb restaurants, I'd rank our dinner as absolutely first-class.

My wife is a native New Englander, and I'm an honorary NE citizen. Our raw bar appetizers and dinner were literally perfect, and on-par with any high-end seafood restaurant I've experienced anywhere. 

J&G made certain that our anniversary dinner was perfect, and we'll return soon!
reviews.author: Dale V.

reviews.text: This place is THE best restaurant in Arizona!!! From the staff to the delicious food! We walked in at 8:30pm & they were closing at 10pm. We sat a table inside the restaurant, but it was too cold for our 9yr old. So the lovely server fetched her a shall to keep her warm. It was so sweet of him to do that. The second server we met set us up with a table outside overlooking Camelback Mountain & the hotel's pool, which was breath taking! There were 2 fire pits outside & it was so beautiful. The food was out of this world! I had a bone in filet mignon, daughter ordered the parmesan crusted chicken and my hubby ordered the lobster tail. The best sides were the asparagus risotto and the Yukon gold mashed potatoes! For appetizers you must try the jumbo shrimp cocktail the east side oysters which were so scrumptious! I could've eaten them all day. This restaurant is gorgeous! The staff go over & beyond to make you happy & so effortless! Every single one of them were in a good mood & so hospitable. Our server was Kandice (hope I spelled it correct), Chris and 2 others that helped out. They work as a team and make sure we are all satisfied and happy. One last thing, try the cheesecake & the chocolate lava cake. You will never want to leave because the food & staff were so amazing & out of this world! Thank you to everyone there! I highly recommend trying this place while in Arizona.
reviews.author: Stephanie N.

reviews.text: Great ambiance and views. Cold average steak. Boring chocolate lava cake. I expected more for the $ with my first visit.
reviews.author: Chris M.

reviews.text:
Fancy place inside a golf resort. Just tell the guy at the gate that you're going to the restaurant. Free validated valet parking- get it stamped at the restaurant. 

Prob the best views in phoenix! Be prepared to spend a lot of guap- $$$$$$

Restaurant is located on the  5th floor I believe so take the elevator there. I recommend making reservations ahead of time (just in case).

We got the raw bar for app- it's basically a platter of oysters, mussels, lobster tail. Super fresh! Was it worth $42- prob not. You can def get the same high quality for cheaper somewhere else but people prob come here for the ambiance. We were seated inside so it was kind of hard to see the views but you can go to the balcony (empty areas) and take some pics.

For my entree I got the steak hanger with fries- cooked perfectly for medium rare ($27)- one of the cheaper options on the menu otherwise it can get really pricey. Honestly it was cooked perfectly but that is expected for a nice place like this. Could I get this somewhere else - same quality but cheaper? Yes, def. Like I said you come here for the ambiance and views.

if you're feeling fancy or if you're not paying- def come here!
reviews.author: Jessie H.

reviews.text: This restaurant completely blew me away. I had the hanger steak and the bread. Both were absolutely outstanding! The bread was as good as bread can possibly get and the same for the steak. I chose the hanger steak because it was the half the price of the other steaks and possibly the best steak, although I've never had any other steak there. In addition, the service was as fast as lightning, and I wish I could eat there every night.
reviews.author: Matthew E.

reviews.text:
We had the filet mignon with asparagus. The asparagus was huge! I thought that they were steamed well so that they were still a bit crispy. The filet was wonderful with a slightly firm outside but tender inside. The béarnaise sauce was light and tasty. For dessert we had the chocolate molten lava cake with ice cream. The caramel ice cream was delicious. The molten lava cake was good too and accompanied by a caramel tuile. 

We also ordered the glazed miso mahi mani.  The glaze had a citrus flavor that was a little strong for my taste but it was cooked well.
reviews.author: Kristen L.

reviews.text:
On a recent business trip, our group was set to dine at J&G, we were set up on the beautiful patio overlooking the whole report and a whole lot of Scottsdale, it was stunning.  The interior of the restaurant is dark and sleek - a very cool and sexy take on your traditional stuffy steakhouse.  As the planners of the event, we decided to ditch the group and dine solo in the lounge. This is the area is part of the bar and has low lying seating but is full service.  I had the short rib and brussels sprouts that evening and they were quite good, we also had the truffle cheese appetizers and I probably could have eaten the whole bowl.  For dessert we had the warm chocolate cake, the apple crumble and the passion fruit pavlova....the apple crumble won.
Aside from the patio, food, and looks of this place, the service was very polished and professional and very nice.
If I was in the area again, I would return.
reviews.author: Lisette C.

reviews.text: I arrived here with a large group and we had a wonderful evening. The view of the Valley from the Phoenician is beautiful. The restaurant has beautiful decor and a nice pleasant atmosphere to it. We all ordered our own dish but ended up doing things family style. I ordered the Prime Hanger Streak Frites & Caramelized Brussel Sprouts. The streak was nice and tender and the brussel sprouts were amazing. The server did a good job of making sure everything was perfect for us. Afterwards we ordered a few bottles of wine (they have a nice selection) and enjoyed the view around the fire out on the balcony. We had a lovely evening and I would definitely come back.
reviews.author: Travis T.

reviews.text: Holy cow - this place has served me the best food I have ever eaten in my life.  The mashed potatoes are silky and tastes amazing.  The steak was cooked perfectly.  It cost $300 for me and my wife together but we also had a full bottle of wine which was $120 by itself.  The atmosphere is very nice and the view is great as well.
reviews.author: Marvin H.

reviews.text: The food was mediocre at best. Very bland salmon dish with over cooked Brussels on the side. My GF ordered her filet medium rare which came out medium well. Took us 10 minutes to flag down our server who promptly replaced the steak with another that was also over cooked.   Meanwhile my salmon got cold as I waited for her entree to arrive. Didn't bother to get dessert as we were just disappointed with the experience. Ambience was cool - live guitarist that played very well although we did hear a rendition of Stairway to Heaven. Nevertheless, I wouldn't recommend J&G unless you want low grade food at a mid grade price. There are many other restaurants in the area that I'd recommend over J&G. Try Mastro's. Not sure why I deviated...
reviews.author: Matt C.

reviews.text:
Our family spent a lovely Christmas through New Year holiday at The Phoenician several weeks ago.  

Weeks before arriving at the resort we made reservations for Christmas Eve  at J & G Steakhouse on the property. At the time of the booking through Open Table, I alerted the restaurant that two people in our party required Gluten Free menus.

Upon being seated at our table we reminded the waiter about the dietary restriction of two of our guests. He said that there was no Gluten Free Menu but that the kitchen could probably be able to fix something that would satisfy their needs.  

When rolls were subsequently brought to our table, I asked if they had gluten free rolls available. We had dined at the Terrazzo restaurant on the property the night before and were pleased that gluten free breads were baked fresh there each day. Our waiter rather testily replied that J & G's did not offer such fare and that if we had given them advanced notice of our dietary needs that they would have been able to have the appropriate bread for us.

The point is, the restaurant was notified several weeks prior when the reservation was made regarding the Gluten Free requirements. Furthermore, couldn't the waiter have sent someone from the large staff of servers that evening down the elevator and bring up some gluten free rolls for our Christmas Eve dinner?  

Believe me, we will not go back to J & G Steakhouse ever again. We felt as if we were cattle herded in to be fed Christmas Eve dinner, then ushered out as soon as possible so that the next cattle could take our place.

I might add that our bill that night totaled near $500 for four adults and two children!!!
reviews.author: Laura D.

reviews.text: NYE dinner was excellent. We ordered app for two-- seafood tower. Delicious. For dinner I ordered the filet mignon- cooked to perfection. The baked potato- salt & pepper was the best.
reviews.author: Gina Marie M.

reviews.text:
Check in with the guard and he gives you the option of valet or park your own car. This is a courteous option but valet is the way to go if you have a date.  If you park yourself, it's an interesting adventure with the utility view of the Phoenician, along with leaking couplers, in the Phoenician basement.  It is also a easy misstep to get on the elevator, read the directions on how to get to the Steakhouse, then still do a misstep at the lobby floor. Yes, the directions are to get off the A/B elevators and change to the C/ D elevators.  The look about in the lobby is a TBT with a bit of 70's decor and several furniture pieces, along with the fountain, dating the hotel.

Jump on those elevators and the entrance to the steakhouse is impressive. The first impression is that it's a destination for drinks, and that is also my last impression.

Grab the Jinga matchsticks and the hostess seats you. We have an early dinner time thus we politely haggle for a table a bit closer to the view. Hey, the place is empty! 

Table appears nicely set and the paper placemats appear organic. Wait until the end of the meal when the busboy crumbles the placemat like Denny's and dumps crumbs on the table.

Ah yes the food! Parker Rolls throw back to the hotel decor and actually are stale. The steak tartare is very good but ruined in presentation by serving in a bowl. It is suggested that a flat plate be used and flavorful dressing provided on the side or thickened up a bit and living up the plating. Steaks were underwhelming, especially compared to the competion in this town, and the smaller NY Strip was actually half the thickness of the larger order.  The smaller steak  was overdone for medium rare. Aside from salads, we cheap out with no sides for the meat entree. This option of ordering a la carte for the main dish feels like a stare down between the restaurant and your wallet (Hard to believe that veggies cannot be thrown in with the pricey steak.)

Service was stellar. Wine options reasonable and savagnon blanc chosen was yummy.

Left a comment card with email & phone but it still must be in a paper pile....
reviews.author: Kara Y.

reviews.text:
This is an over top setting steak house. So as usual I will rate them based on the ratings:
Atmosphere: 5
Parking:5
Service:5
Food:2
Value:2

Overall 2. 
The food was just ok, lots of hype around the location and setup. The setting was nice but just did not do it for me.
reviews.author: Rocker 1.

reviews.text: J & G is a 5 star restaurant that I have yet to find anywhere else in Scottsdale that can compare with the ambiance, food and service.  Everyone that I have taken there loves it and always wants to go there for dinner when they're in town visiting us.  I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone that wants to eat at a classy place.
reviews.author: MR. M.

reviews.text: My husband and I have been here several times and have not once had anything less than amazing service and excellent food. Friendly, accommodating staff makes the evening a little extra special. The atmosphere is quiet, romantic and perfect for a date night or special celebration.
reviews.author: Annette K.

reviews.text: Very disappointed.  Poor service never saw a waiter till after seated for 20 minutes.  Ordered the thanksgiving dinner and it was so dry you couldn't eat it.  Understand that demand is high on thanksgiving but would never go back.
reviews.author: Nancy V.

reviews.text: This was our first and last visit at J and G. The ONLY thing  this restaurant has in its favor is the ambiance. In that regard it is a 5 star. It stops there. The Server was abrupt and defensive. Different servers bringing side dishes were untimely. Salads were salty, the steaks were dry with no taste, side order of mushrooms had an odd taste, rolls were white bread, shrimp cocktail had small shrimp and each steak sauce (3) was worse than the next. The French fries were cold and the mashed potatoes were overly salty.  I was amazed that such a beautiful resort would have such inferior food and service. Other than the terrific ambiance, I can't think of one thing positive regarding the food or service. In total, this was an unbelievably BAD experience. They did take back the salad and fries however the server was argumentative that he sees the kitchen staff making the fries daily. Amazing........I am speechless.
reviews.author: mark k.

reviews.text: Amazing food and service here! The views were breathtaking. We started off with the black truffle cheese fritters, which pops in your mouth, crunchy and then melts. The prime ribeye steak was cooked to perfection! Grilled and nicely charred on the outside, and juicy and tender on the inside. The potatoes au gratin were good too. The entire Phoenician resort had awesome views. Love this place!
reviews.author: Thoui L.

reviews.text: Great ambience. Sub par service. My porterhouse steak was ok. Tried my wife's steak the NY strip which was pretty good. If I want to have a great steak I will go somewhere else like Ruths Chris or elsewhere. The appetizers were excellent. We got the tuna tartare and truffle cheese fritters. Small serving size but very tasty. I agree the chocolate molten cake with the caramel ice cream was excellent but nothing unique.
reviews.author: Nadeem H.

reviews.text: View and atmosphere are great. The main server was nice, though it seems there were different people assigned for bread vs drinks vs actual bringing out of the dishes. Drink refills were slow, but the server was so polite it was easy to forgive. Our table had to wait 45 minutes to get our food, so I guess I recommend ordering appetizers to hold you over until your main dish arrives. Overall the food was quite enjoyable.
reviews.author: Esther T.

reviews.text: Amazing food, view and service. Will definitely come back for the next special occasion.
reviews.author: Scott G.

reviews.text: All time favorite. Great service and everything was beyond delicious and cooked to perfection.  I only wish that I could afford to dine there more often!!!  Treat yourself and go!!!
reviews.author: One W.

reviews.text: I wanted to message the management directly but there is no option on the website so I will post here. Simply put the most disappointing "nice" meal I've ever had. Started with the "jumbo" shrimp app which was far from jumbo. Also had the oysters which were decent and onion soup which was pretty good. Then we had the ny strip which came out at room temperature and was just not good. Ordered it medium and wasn't pink at all. We had a 945 reservation which was their last so clearly wanted to close. Dee like they cooked steak when we ordered apps and just let it sit in the window. My girlfriend had the lobster which was very good. We also had the Brussels sprouts which I couldn't bare to eat. Our waiter couldn't have been nicer he was great! Overall just a very below average meal and not worth the money.
reviews.author: David F.

reviews.text: A dinner here is a terrific experience in all respects. (To truly make an evening of it, you'll want to start with a cocktail or four in the Thirsty Camel lounge downstairs.) Upstairs, the sleek bar makes great cocktails and has vases of fresh herbs at hand to add the extra sparkle. Service is very smooth and accommodating; I've always been made to feel very welcome and I've always had the impression they really care about providing a great dining experience. And of course, the view over the valley from this high perch is pretty amazing. As this is a big dining room, of course not all tables are going to have the up-close windowside view, so you might want to come on an off-peak night if you're dying for that. There's plenty of space in the bar area to get a nice long look if your table is further back. On my most recent visit, I had the signature charred corn ravioli in a basil fondue ($11), and it was heavenly as always, and the perfect size for an appetizer. I followed that up with the NY steak, a perfectly-cooked (medium rare) 10 oz portion ($39) that came with a choice of sauces. I picked the sweet onion-chili, which was a great tangy/spicy combo. After I had placed my order, I decided I had a hankering for some melted bleu cheese on the steak so I asked the waiter if they could accommodate. It was no problem and very nicely done. For dessert, I had the ice cream and sorbet selection--and you can choose your combinations and how many scoops you want to customize the size. For a restaurant of this quality in a resort this well-known, and with a name-chef as the owner, the prices are pretty darn reasonable. I can eat better here for less than I can at the Ruth's Chris at home, so I really can't find fault here.
reviews.author: Adam B.

reviews.text:
Ok...so I really hate writing a bad review. After all it's only one meal in a sea of meals over a lifetime. But we were so disappointed in our dinner at J&G I just can't let it slide. 
First, the service was pretty good. Not great, but good. Our lead server was noticeably cool when we didn't order wine with dinner. We had just come from an event in the hotel (Phoenician) and had already drank a couple of glasses. And besides, we had heard so many good things about J&G from the hotel staff (not so much on Yelp) that we wanted to enjoy the food without being impaired. 
The low down:
We ordered the tasting menu for $80 each. It started with a civeche  (sp) that was way over salted. 
The next course was a corn ravioli. It was fair, but pretty bland 
Next came the crusted halibut. Probably the best course and perfectly done. 
Then came the Wagu steak. It may or may not been Wagu, but my opinion is it was not! Absolutely a low grade steak that was in sufficiently seasoned and should have been seared. 
I would definitely skip this joint. El Terrazzo is much better in the hotel. Or go into Scottsdale and enjoy Wild Fish.
reviews.author: Leroy N.

reviews.text: Horrible.  Filet was dry and chewy.  Calamari was way over salted.  Asparagus soggy.  My date had the salmon which was just ok.  Service was terrible.  Waiter was unrefined, didn't know product, wine list, and sneezed as he brought our food to the table.  He belongs at a Denny's not a high end restaurant.  Ambience great, but food was truly one if the worst meals I have had.  Took only two bites of steak.  Left early, didn't even finish wine.  Intolerable
reviews.author: Brian n.

reviews.text:
The food was pretty good especially the rib eye, but unfortunately I won't be back due to the 50 min wait on our entrees'! It wouldn't have been so bad if there weren't less than 20 ppl in the restaurant & a couple who was seated AFTER we ordered our food was served their food 25 min before us. They also had steak! Lol! Our waiter never came to offer any explanation or recognize the wait, until we sort of grabbed him rushing by & then he offered an apology & went to see why. I always order my steak medium so that wasn't the reason, but whatever the reason, which was never given,
I won't be returning, there are toooooo many other GREAT steak houses in Phoenix!
reviews.author: Mrs. M.

reviews.text:
Very good! 
I had the 5 course tasting menu, my husband had the summer run special and our 3 year old had the steak frites. We also had a couple oysters to start. Everything was DELICIOUS! 
Will return the next time we are here!
reviews.author: Kristin W.

reviews.text: Beautiful view. The 40 dollar menu was excellent, the ravioli was incredible and so was the flank steak and the chocolate cake and caramel ice cream for dessert. A very good deal.
reviews.author: Rossana N.

reviews.text:
1 star and they don't even deserve that.  The combination of p*ss poor customer service and mediocre food leaves me never wanting to come back.  We attended this place on July 3rd and had a reservation at 9:00.  I requested a booth a week in advance, but they couldn't even accommodate that.   Let's just get straight to the review.

Food/Service

Our waiter was no were to be seen most of the night.  We ordered a few drinks and couple of appetizers to start.  Black Truffle cheese fritters and calamari.  Both were ok, and the portions are a joke.  Most nice restaurants serve some sort of calamari dish and for what you pay here is down right insulting.  There were probably 6 to 7 pieces, seriously WTF.  For dinner we order the Filet Mignon and porterhouse steak.  My fiancee requested it medium well and I wanted my steak medium rare.  Her steak was served rare and mine was overcooked on the medium well side.  SMH.  Our sides were a potato gratin and creamed corn dish.  Once again they serve it in a little dish and the flavors were nothing special.  Our waiter said he would bring us out bread, but that never happened.  I had to request my coke to be filled up several times and had to stack the dirty plates for them to finally take it away.  Seriously, where is the customer service?  I snapped couple of pics, didn't even want to waste my time, but posting anyway.

Not the most memorable nice dinners I've had in a while.  For the food that they serve they are not an elite or top steakhouse in the valley.  They are more like a Keg's Steakhouse, Longhorns, or Flemings.  For a great steak and experience, I would recommend Mastro's, Dominick's (Scottsdale Quarter) or Donovan's.

Report Card=F!!!
reviews.author: Thomas L.

reviews.text:
Made a reservation through Open Table and requested a nice view for our anniversary. We were immediately seated and brought to a table with a large panoramic window. Perfect! 

The $40 summer sunset menu is pre-fixed and includes a three course meal. We chose asparagus as an appetizer, the slow cooked salmon as an entree and the warm chocolate cake with caramel ice cream for dessert. The asparagus was alright -- came in four our five stems, but nothing to rave about like the salmon and chocolate cake. The salmon was cooked perfectly...not one bit of dryness. Real tender and a pretty good size. The chocolate cake was amazing. Coupled with the caramel ice cream, it is a perfect dessert. I don't have much of a sweet tooth. This dessert is not overly sweet and it just melts in your mouth. Thanks J&G for the "Happy Anniversary" greeting drizzled on our dessert plate...

We also got the 19 ounce rib eye ($ 60) to share. Again, cooked perfectly medium as requested. Real juicy and flavorful already. J&G offers sauces for your steak. As first timers, we did not know which to select. Our server kindly brought us a sample of the three most popular choices. In our opinion (from the three we tried), the best was the black pepper. Second was the chili glaze and third was the J&G steak sauce. Nice touch with the sauce condiment option...

Our server was very attentive and the manager came around to follow up with us as well. Along with the beers that we ordered (good selection of craft beer bottles at J&G), our dinner came out to $150 (total including tax and tip). Very great deal for a very full, satisfying meal for two with an amazing view and top notch service. Next time we are in Scottsdale, we'll definitely be back!
reviews.author: Gail A.

reviews.text: if you ever want to go to a good steak house, don't ever go to J&G...,horribly understaffed and inattentive...,,you would get better service at Pizza Hut
reviews.author: Thomas E.

reviews.text: Delicious. Amazing food and service. It is kind of pricy but we'll be back for sure. I had lamb shank and my wife had the salmon. It was cooked to the order. You should try the calamari with the Rosemary aioli for sure. The best.
reviews.author: Sensei M.

reviews.text: My husband and I ate here last night for our anniversary. The room, atmosphere, and views were awesome. The service was mediocre. The person who seemed to be the sommelier or wine director didn't know much about wine in general or the wines on the list, which was surprising at a restaurant like this. Our dinner took a really, really long time. The oysters were excellent but the rest of our food was just ok. I ordered an heirloom tomato salad, which was good, but it had onion rings on top which made no sense at all. I love onion rings- just didn't go together. I've had better steak other places. Overall, it's worth going for the view but don't expect great food. There are definitely better placed to eat in Scottsdale.
reviews.author: Dana H.

reviews.text: The ginger margarita is not to be missed. We ordered a Porterhouse for sharing with sweet snap peas and roasted beets. The steak was flavorful and didn't need the variety of sauces but we tried all of them anyway. The J&G steak sauce had a star anise flavor in the back end of the palette, simply curious in the taste buds. The interiors were classy yet modern, the variety of seating gives a certain feeling of privacy. The server's attention to detail makes you feel special. The amuse-bouche had a hint of truffle that teased my appetite.
reviews.author: Jhoiey R.

reviews.text: Gorgeous views, exceptional service, amazing food. We chose the tasting menu and loved every course. The entire night was fun and this place is not stuffy or uptight.
reviews.author: Margaret B.

reviews.text: Have to lower my rating on this place after last night. We have eaten here dozens of times of the years and last night we took friends here for a birthday dinner. Everything we excellent except my filet which was to be cooked medium, it came out DONE, I mean really done as in grey all the way through. About half way through dinner the host came by and ask how if everything was alright I pointed out my over cooked uneaten steak. They offered to replace it but at that point everyone would have been done eating by the time it arrived so I declined. They were very prompt in removing it from the bill and the waiter apologized for it, I pointed out it was not his fault, kitchen mistakes happen so they handled it correctly. Over all we had a nice evening, the bill at $250 including drinks and tip was very fair and we will be back.
reviews.author: Jt C.

reviews.text:
I dined here on with my wife to celebrate our anniversary, we were at table 47 on 4/18/15. The service was extremely slow and my wife's filet was overcooked. The waiter was hard to find even to fill up water.
Not even once did anyone come by to see if our meal was ok and needed anything. My wife barely touched anything on the plate and when they came to take it away, since we had not seen our waiter I asked for the check and a manager. The only thing I received was the check, which took so long my wife finally left the table and went to the bar to have a drink while I waited.
When I paid the bill and went to the bar, my wife had been waiting there for over ten minutes and had still had not even been acknowledged. Apparently one of the bartenders was in labor so they were short staffed, however many servers and hostess were standing around nearby doing nothing.
I called twice the following week to speak with a manager and never received a call back, so this posting is a result of a complete lack of accountability and care from the management.
We chose J & G because it was one of the only "high end" steakhouses we had not been to before in the metro area.
We will never return and I would recommend avoiding it, it may be good much of the time but if there is a problem it certainly will not be addressed. A complete waste of money and more importantly it was for a special occasion.
There are many better places to have a great steak, outside of the view, this was a terrible experience.
reviews.author: Tom W.

reviews.text:
Located in the Phoenician resort in the former Mary Elaine's space. Obviously, the views are still incredible both from inside as well as from the balcony that also has fire pits to prolong the night.
While not as over the top as Mary Elaine's, it is not just a steak house like Mastro's, Ruth Chris or Mortons. We ordered wine from the impressive wine list and started out with the calamari as an appetizer. It was lightly fried and finished with lemon and some spices.
Our group all opted for the filets, along with one selection of the Dover Sole.
The service was good and attentive but without being too meddlesome.
Not a cheap date but a good spot for a special occasion.
reviews.author: Jack N.

reviews.text: Not going to lie. Was not impressed. The waiter was pretty bad. He messed up on dinner and really never came back to the table I asked him to snap a picture and acted annoyed we asked me to do so.... Weird because at resort Oysters were average at best and salad literally had two trips of bacon on top. Wine and drinks decent but can't say anything else that impressed me. My company was out this world but I'd try MASTROS or something else. Thumbs down for sure.
reviews.author: Melissa H.

reviews.text: Recently dined there for a Birthday dinner. Not our first time at the Phoenician, but our first time at John George. Service was fantastic, views of the valley awesome and the food selection and quality were amazing! Overall ambience of the dining area was great. Terrific lighting and while the restaurant was busy, there was still a nice touch of intimate, romantic dining. My bone-in rib eye was cooked and seasoned perfectly. Will definitely go back . . .
reviews.author: Darrell M.

reviews.text: Seriously great steak! I had the filet mignon, and it was 8oz of savory goodness. With bernaise sauce, of course! Even the fried calamari for an appetizer was ON POINT, unlike any other calamari I've ever had. If you're looking for a tasty drink to go along with all of that, try the signature Dark and Stormy. Beyond amazing dinner and dessert - I can't wait to come back!
reviews.author: Jenna C.

reviews.text:
The outside view was very nice.
The food was alright. Nothing outstanding. The calamari was bland & the sauce didn't quite go well with it, not to mention the portion size was small. 
Our food came out very late too, entres & appetizers included. 
Was expecting a better experience based on the high price but felt disappointed.
reviews.author: Kayla T.

reviews.text: I just want to start off by saying amazing service! I took my girlfriend and I out for dinner for an early valentine's and they treated us like royalty. The view from our table was gorgeous, the live music was soothing and very romantic, waiter was very professional and answered all of our questions, he welcomed us for it being our first time here and he  recommended items. Food was outstanding (I had the porterhouse, girlfriend had then filet) all in all they have an outstanding staff, I had a great experience from the time I was greeted at the gate and wished a happy valentine's day to when I picked up my car down stairs. Definitely coming back.
reviews.author: David L.

reviews.text: We were sat at our table and it took over 5 minutes before we were greeted by our waiter"Padrick".  The food was excellent however the waiter had a bit of an attitude problem.  I understand he works in a high end eatery and deals with pampas assholes but he shouldn't treat his guest like one.  "Padrick" might want to check his attitude at home or find another career.  The rest of the Phoenician resort was extremely polite and courteous!
reviews.author: Jen M.

reviews.text: My fiancé and I went here for our anniversary just last week. We were really excited considering the stellar reviews it has gotten. However, our service was fair at best, and the food was nothing to brag about. She got the filet and I got the 24oz porterhouse. My porterhouse had a lot of fat, but her filet was actually really tender. We also ordered three appetizers and drinks and all of it did not match the pricey bill at the end.
reviews.author: Jeremy D.

reviews.text: Perfect place for romantic dinner. Great live music on Fridays and Saturdays. Tuna tartar a must. The steaks great but the Béarnaise sauce was wow. Wine list good. Overall amazing dinner a great place a night out with your loved one.
reviews.author: Jason C.

reviews.text: This place has the worst service I've ever seen in my entire life. I sat down at 7 with my family for my beautiful mothers birthday. It is now 9 and our food hasn't even come to the table. Also the waitress spilled a drink all over the person next to us. This place is horrible every time I come the food is decent at best for a restaurant that is supposed to be this nice. And the 2 hour wait definitely doesn't make it worth it.
